messages.subject: Re: Connecting shiny apps.io to local computer via Socket Client
parts:
In order for an application hosted on shinyapps.io to connect to a remote server, whether a database or another type of application, that remote server must be accessible from the internet and allow traffic from our servers' IP addresses (listed in section 3.8.3 of the user guide).

If you share a bit more about your situation, I could try to make a recommendation about what to do.

messages.subject: Re: Connecting shiny apps.io to local computer via Socket Client
parts:
I'm still trying to connect Shinyapps.io to an application running on my local workstation.  Here's the situation:  I'm using an API in my shinyapps.io application to connect with the application Trader Workstation (tws) running on my local machine.  With Trader Workstation running, I can send queries to get real time stock market data.  When I run the shiny app on my local workstation, it works fine.  Here's the server side call with a data request to tws:
  server <- (function(input, output) 
  {output$ticker <- renderText({input$ticker})
  output$OHLC <- renderText({
    OHLC <- reqHistoricalData(tws, twsEquity(input$ticker), "20160908 16:00:00", "1 day","1 D")})})

The API uses ActiveX and Socket Clients, with my socket port 7496.  What other information would you need to let me know how to connect shinyapps.io to the local workstation?

messages.author: 299a5089d6c6c523
messages.subject: Re: Connecting shiny apps.io to local computer via Socket Client
parts:
The server you want to connect to needs to be available on the internet and accept incoming connections on port 7496 from the IP addresses of shinyapps.io.
If you are talking about a home computer, you will likely have to configure your router to port forward to your computer.
If you are talking about a company, you will likely need to speak with your IT department.

You can test that you have it set up correctly by using a web tool such as http://www.uptimeinspector.com/test-server-connection.html (select "custom port", enter the address of your server, and 7496 for the port)

Once you have that set up, instead of using "localhost", your R code would use address of your server.

On Friday, September 9, 2016 at 4:14:48 PM UTC-4, Scott Novogoratz wrote:
I'm still trying to connect Shinyapps.io to an application running on my local workstation.  Here's the situation:  I'm using an API in my shinyapps.io application to connect with the application Trader Workstation (tws) running on my local machine.  With Trader Workstation running, I can send queries to get real time stock market data.  When I run the shiny app on my local workstation, it works fine.  Here's the server side call with a data request to tws:
  server <- (function(input, output) 
  {output$ticker <- renderText({input$ticker})
  output$OHLC <- renderText({
    OHLC <- reqHistoricalData(tws, twsEquity(input$ticker), "20160908 16:00:00", "1 day","1 D")})})

The API uses ActiveX and Socket Clients, with my socket port 7496.  What other information would you need to let me know how to connect shinyapps.io to the local workstation?


On Tuesday, September 6, 2016 at 8:29:04 AM UTC-6, Joshua Spiewak wrote:
In order for an application hosted on shinyapps.io to connect to a remote server, whether a database or another type of application, that remote server must be accessible from the internet and allow traffic from our servers' IP addresses (listed in section 3.8.3 of the user guide).

If you share a bit more about your situation, I could try to make a recommendation about what to do.
